claims.claim: Epiphanius of Salamis was the bishop of Salamis, Cyprus, at the end of the 4th century.
Epiphanius was born c. 310–320 in Judea and died in 403 at sea.
Epiphanius was nominated and consecrated as Bishop of Salamis, Cyprus, in 365 or 367, a post which he held until his death.
Epiphanius served as bishop for nearly forty years.
Epiphanius was also the Metropolitan of the Church of Cyprus.
Epiphanius gained a reputation as a strong defender of orthodoxy.
Epiphanius is best known for composing the Panarion, a compendium of eighty heresies.
The Anaphora Graeca contains eucharistic prayer language including the words of institution for the bread and wine.
Epiphanius studied and practiced monasticism in Egypt.
Epiphanius's chief target was the teachings of Origen, whom he considered more a Greek philosopher than a Christian.
Epiphanius was born at Besanduk, near Eleutheropolis, in Judea, after 310.
